clue.text: Official on course or attendant in mess?

definitions.meaning: an official who enforces the rules at a racecourse meeting
a mess ... serves food and drink in a military or ship's mess

explanation.surface: Someone at the races, or a servant in a muddle, is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like disorder, but it is the dining room of soldiers or sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the racing official and the dining-room attendant share the job title, so either sense fits.

clue.text: Make low attack in first RAF exercise

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Air force trainees practise a ground attack in their first drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the answer spanning firST RAF Exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Endless joy seen in swallow? One born to fly

indicators.note: seen in places the shortened joy word within the swallow word

parts.note: to eat is to swallow

indicators.note: endless means with its final letter cut off

parts.note: glee is joy

explanation.surface: A happy swallow suggests a bird made for flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb. 'Endless' drops the last letter of the joy word; 'seen in' places the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a chick destined to soar.

clue.text: Coal: an ancient land imports it

indicators.note: imports means brings in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: Thrace was an ancient region north of the Aegean
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old country brings in coal from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imports' signals insertion; Thrace was the ancient land of the north Aegean, now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is a hard, high-carbon variety of coal.

clue.text: Avoid Venetian magistrate incarcerating 500

indicators.note: incarcerating means locking up, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Steer clear of a Venetian official who jails five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incarcerating' puts D inside DOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade or sidestep, the same as avoid.

clue.text: English company in Knock shows propriety

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviations sit within the word for knock

parts.note: to drum is to knock or beat repeatedly

explanation.surface: An English firm behaves correctly when hit by bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' is not a blow of misfortune here but a verb meaning to beat; 'in' puts the abbreviations inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is correct, seemly behaviour, a close synonym of propriety.

clue.text: Wild flower: give to old drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pass a wild bloom to an inebriated elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GIVE TO OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog violet is a common unscented violet found growing wild in woods and hedges.

clue.text: Fetching chopped artichoke at last

parts.note: cut means chopped

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the vegetable

explanation.surface: Fetching some sliced artichoke, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' seems to mean bringing, but it is the adjective for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching and cute both mean attractive or charming in appearance.

clue.text: See Romeo's revolutionary supporter for bigger prize

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lover is a supporter or fan, as in a music lover

explanation.surface: Romeo's radical admirer is noticed seeking a bigger reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns LO and R round to make ROL. Romeo suggests Shakespeare's lover, but he only supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollover is a lottery jackpot carried forward unwon, so the next prize is larger.

clue.text: Accomplished as male teacher?

definitions.meaning: a master is a male schoolteacher, so ... read literally means in the manner of one

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer literally: MASTER plus -LY, like a schoolmaster; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterly describes work showing great skill, so it means accomplished.

clue.text: Morally correct ceremony for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so we want a word that sounds like the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a religious or formal ceremony

explanation.surface: A ceremony shown on television is deemed ethically proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals a word spoken: RITE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Right as an adjective means just or ethical, the same as morally correct.

clue.text: Understand Europeans banning a new drug

parts.note: dig is slang for understand, as in 'I dig it'

indicators.note: banning means excluding, so certain letters are kept out of the word for Europeans

parts.note: Italians are Europeans
a gives A and N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Continental authorities forbidding a novel medicine is something you grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' takes A and N out of ITALIANS, leaving ITALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, from foxglove, is a heart medication, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Bloom shows full desire uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flower reveals an overwhelming longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrollably' shuffles the letters of FULL DESIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is a stylised lily or iris, a flower, so a bloom.

clue.text: Spot unwanted garden visitor

definitions.meaning: a small dark spot on the skin
a burrowing animal whose hills ruin lawns

explanation.surface: One notices an intruder in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a verb, to see, but it is a noun: a skin blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mole names both a skin blemish and the tunnelling mammal gardeners dislike.

clue.text: Aunt's dog in wild really impressive

indicators.note: wild suggests running out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A relative's dog running free is a remarkable sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges AUNTSDOGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means amazing or astonishing, so very impressive.

clue.text: A cold fish admitting she has fatal flaw

parts.note: a chill is a cold, the minor illness

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word is taken inside the others

parts.note: the eel is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unfeeling woman confesses to a weakness that will be her undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cold fish' reads as an unfeeling person, but splits into three pieces; 'admitting' takes the pronoun in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero Achilles could be wounded only in his heel, so the phrase means a single fatal weakness.

clue.text: Ancient Hebrew realities distorted

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Truths about the past have been twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges REALITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew nation descended from Jacob.

clue.text: Assist old boy with raincoat going up country

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means assist
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

explanation.surface: Help a former pupil with his raincoat as he climbs out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses AIDOBMAC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Female, let down, prospered

parts.note: to let down is to lower

explanation.surface: A woman who was disappointed went on to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let down' reads as disappointed, but here it means lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowered in the figurative sense means flourished or blossomed, i.e. thrived.

clue.text: Nothing but repetition? Rather regular repetition maybe!

definitions.note: the phrase itself repeats its initial R sound, an example of the device

parts.note: all means only or nothing but, as in 'all talk'
iteration is repetition

explanation.surface: A wry remark on a clue that seems to be nothing but repeated words.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example of the answer: three words starting with R. 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliteration is the repetition of an initial sound, and 'Rather regular repetition' shows exactly that.

clue.text: Despot left in dishonour

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the dishonour word

parts.note: a stain is a blot on one's reputation, a dishonour

explanation.surface: A tyrant has been abandoned in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute tyrant.

clue.text: Strike's ending: Unite creates issue

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of the strike word

parts.note: to merge is to unite

explanation.surface: As a walkout ends, the trade union Unite causes a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Unite is also the name of a big British trade union, which fits the strike story. 'issue' is a verb, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out or flow forth, which is what emerge means.

clue.text: Black bird in wood

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
the owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird perches in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game of bowls, the balls are traditionally called woods, so 'wood' is not a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl in lawn bowls is called a wood, as it was originally made of lignum vitae.

clue.text: Spy one-time GP playing on piano

indicators.note: on here means placed after the piano letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about and being reset

explanation.surface: A retired family doctor is at the keyboard performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ONETIMEGP, and 'on' puts that after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur who secretly watches others, so he spies on them.

clue.text: Old man outside with forest creature

indicators.note: outside means the father word goes around the other piece

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
and means with or together with

explanation.surface: Dad is out with a woodland animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' gives a word of its own, not just a link; 'outside' wraps the father round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda lives in the mountain bamboo forests of China.

clue.text: Closely examine small container

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Look carefully at a little box.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan can mean to scrutinise thoroughly, though it also means to glance.

clue.text: Management course

definitions.meaning: the guiding or managing of something

explanation.walkthrough: Two plain senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction covers both leadership of an enterprise and the bearing one travels along.

clue.text: Lazybones unusually riled

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A layabout gets oddly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges RILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is a slacker who avoids work, which is what an idler does.

clue.text: Article by poet a slow piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by a poet is a leisurely composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is the grammatical kind, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An andante is a musical movement played at a moderately slow, walking tempo.

clue.text: Gas connected to north-eastern French region

parts.note: argon is an inert gas

explanation.surface: A gas pipeline is linked to an area in north-east France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north-eastern' looks like it describes the region, but it only supplies NE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonne is a forested area of north-eastern France, famous for First World War battles.
